title: The Quartet
text:
A mischievous monkey, a donkey, a goat and a clumsy bear decided to form a string quartet. They got hold of music and instruments, a pair of violins, a viola and a cello, and sat down in a meadow under a lime tree to charm the world with their art.

They began to play, and the noise was dreadful. They stopped. The monkey had an idea: the trouble must be how they were sitting. The bear with the cello should face the viola, and the first violin should sit across from the second. They rearranged themselves and began again. It was just as bad.

They argued and moved their seats again and again. Then the donkey announced that he had the answer: they should all sit in a row. They tried that, and the noise did not improve.

At last they noticed a nightingale in the tree and asked him to settle the matter. How should they sit to play well? The nightingale answered that to be musicians, one needs skill and a finer ear than theirs. And you, my friends, however you sit, he said, you still will not be musicians.
lesson: Reorganizing a team cannot replace the skills it lacks. Before changing the structure again, ask whether the people have what the work requires.
people: A monkey, a donkey, a goat, a bear, a nightingale
